source.title: The Elicitation Game: Evaluating Capability Elicitation Techniques
source.authors: Felix Hofstätter; Teun van der Weij; Jayden Teoh; Rada Djoneva; Henning Bartsch; F. Ward

record.tranche_reason: Tests elicitation of deliberately hidden capabilities in password-locked and circuit-broken model organisms, rather than testing unlearning methods on unlearned models.
record.gate_note: The study tests prompting and fine-tuning attacks on synthetic hidden-capability models. It does not apply gradient-ascent unlearning, Who's Harry Potter, RMU, or other unlearning methods. It also tests activation steering by adding vectors, not direction ablation. The paper's discussion of unlearning is background, not a result.
record.test_reason: No unlearning method is applied or evaluated. The study deliberately inserts hidden capabilities (password-locking, then circuit-breaking) and tests eliciting them. That is induced concealment, not knowledge removal by unlearning. Unlearning and WMDP appear only as related work and benchmark source. WMDP is used purely as a question set. No row measures recovery of knowledge removed by an unlearning method, and circuit-breaking here is not a counter-method to unlearning attacks.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Also: combined prompting (N-shot plus prefilling) elicits MCQA capability from both model organisms; steering is less effective, failing on circuit-broken models and APPS; and circuit-breaking was fragile to hyperparameters.
record.recipe_differences: Creates synthetic hidden-capability models using password-locking, then circuit-breaking; it does not apply an unlearning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Elicitation effectiveness varies by model, benchmark, and model-organism construction. Circuit-breaking is reported as sensitive to training hyperparameters. Combining prefilling and N-shot prompting often improves results; on APPS prompting is much less effective than on MCQA.

fits_no_version.finding: Password-locked capabilities on WMDP, MMLU and APPS are recovered by SFT and by unrelated anti-refusal training, and mostly by N-shot plus prefilling prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Capabilities deliberately hidden by password-locking fine-tuning remain elicitable by fine-tuning and by combined prompting.

fits_no_version.finding: Circuit-breaking applied after password-locking resists single prompting methods, especially for Mistral and for APPS. Fine-tuning and anti-refusal still recover the capability, and combined prompts recover MCQA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-level (circuit-breaking) concealment resists prompt elicitation more than output-level locking, but not fine-tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267 (2025)
record.problems: Evidence comes from deliberately constructed password-locked and circuit-broken model organisms, not models subjected to unlearning. The study uses relatively small models and limited benchmarks. Circuit-breaking is described as fragile to training hyperparameters. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Activation-steering addition results are discussed and shown in figures, but they do not test the direction-ablation or deletion-versus-access claims. Other steering results and standalone prefilling values are not included as rows here; the record prioritizes fine-tuning and prompting recovery results relevant to versions B and E.

untested.parts: No relearning on unlearned models; fine-tuning targets password-locked capabilities.
No direction ablation, and no analysis of unlearning.
Prompting targets password-locked models, not unlearned ones.
Circuit-breaking hides an inserted capability; it is not an unlearning counter-method.

record.verdict_notes: This is a sandbagging/elicitation study on backdoor model organisms. It is relevant by analogy only: hidden-but-present capability versus removed capability. All row version tags (V2/V5/V6) were invalid and are reset to none. The reader's T3/tests judgement is overturned under the rule excluding deliberately induced behaviour.

versions.untested_parts: No unlearning method is tested, and the study does not assess retaining general ability while unlearning targeted knowledge.

The size of the fine-tuning set is not stated here; the study does not establish that only a small relearning set is needed. SFT uses capability-related demonstrations, while anti-refusal training is unrelated to the target capability.
No activation direction is ablated, and the study does not establish that an unlearning method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests few-shot prompting, response prefilling, and multi-turn requests; does not test prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks as such, other languages, or adding in-context information after actual unlearning.

Tests circuit-breaking in synthetic model organisms against some elicitation techniques, not a counter-method to unlearning on real unlearned models; does not show resistance to all attacks listed in the claim.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Supervised fine-tuning on WMDP and MMLU model organisms
reader_labels.reason: SFT reaches or exceeds the with-password reference in most reported settings; r1-r3 and r5-r12. Fine-tuning-set size is not stated.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Anti-refusal training on APPS password-locked and circuit-broken Gemma-instruct
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that unrelated anti-refusal training elicited full hidden code-generation capability; r43-r44.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Password-locked MCQA models, especially with prefilling combined with few-shot prompts
reader_labels.reason: Combined prompting reaches or nearly reaches the with-password reference across the reported WMDP and MMLU conditions; r19, r21, r23, r31, r33, r35.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Circuit-broken MCQA models and APPS code generation
reader_labels.reason: Prompting recovery varies by model and task: circuit-broken Mistral MCQA scores remain low in several conditions, and APPS prompting/multi-turn results are far below full capability; r14, r16, r18, r20, r22, r26, r28, r30, r32, r34, r39-r42.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Circuit-breaking often reduces elicitation, particularly for Mistral models, but combined prompts recover near-full MMLU performance for Gemma-instruct and substantial WMDP performance in some cases; r14, r16, r18, r20, r22, r24, r26, r28, r30, r32, r34, r36.
